_doc: bugs_open/358 — one entry per agent_error_log error_code. THE AUTHORITY IS THE LIVE TABLE, not this file and not a source scan: `config-key-audit --finding-codes` reads SELECT DISTINCT error_code and asks whether each observed code is declared here. That is deliberate — agenterrors.Write calls itself 'The ONE writer against agent_error_log' and it is NOT (four of five INSERT paths bypass it, and internal/agents/contentcreator CANNOT use it: *pgxpool.Pool against a *sql.DB parameter), so a check anchored on the seam or on a grep would read clean while most writers walked past. KEYED ON THE CODE UP TO THE FIRST COLON (358 §8: error_code is free text and one writer emits colon-suffixed variants); raw_variants lists what is actually written, so a family cannot double-count as compliance. DISPOSITIONS: consumed (an automated reader selects by this code and acts — `reader` must be a file:line the checker verifies CONTAINS the code, AND `reader_sink` must name the TABLE that reader selects it from, which the checker verifies the reader file mentions); instrumented (deliberate, time-boxed measurement — `owner` doc and a `review_by` date the checker expires); human-evidence (hand-run forensics only — `why` must name the retention window it accepts); operational (failure plumbing, whose correct consumption IS the generic newest-N diagnostic read — 358 §2.3); unruled (declared, not yet decided — a COUNTED BACKLOG, listed at exit 0, never an exemption). Every required field is chosen so it cannot be satisfied by typing, which is RFC_029 §10.15's lesson from optional_explicit_wire_acks.json: 'an ack satisfiable by typing the key is no ack'. AN OBSERVED CODE ABSENT FROM THIS FILE IS A FINDING (exit 1). A registered code NOT observed is report-only — retention is 30 days, so absence proves 30 days and never 'never'. ⚠ STATED LIMIT: `consumed` says a reader selects by this code and acts on it. It does NOT say the WRITER can see the whole population it would need to — a detector that only fires on one code path is blind to everything off it, however faithfully its rows are read (worked example: STRUCTURAL_KEY_CARRY_MISS below). Coverage of the writer is a separate question this registry does not answer and must not be read as answering. ⚠ SECOND STATED LIMIT, and a DIFFERENT one (added 2026-08-23): `consumed` also used to be silently ambiguous about WHICH SINK the reader reads. component_validation_rejected has a genuine automated reader — migration 563 branches the component-creator's prompt on the failure class — but that reader reads `site_work_items.retry_feedback` (single writer: store_generated_component_action.go:1587, wired by 564), NOT this table. Its agent_error_log row is a PARALLEL record nothing reads. Marked `consumed` it would have passed the reader check (563 does contain the string) and read as a closed loop for ever. Hence `reader_sink`: a value other than `agent_error_log` is REPORTED, not failed — a parallel append-only record beside an overwritten column is often deliberate — but it can never again read as though THIS table's row were consumed. The check's own limit, stated: it proves the reader file MENTIONS the sink, not that it selects this code from it; a file naming several tables can satisfy it wrongly.
_unruled_cap_doc: THE RATCHET (owner ruling 2026-08-23: cap it). The unruled count may never EXCEED this number — a new code parked rather than decided is a FINDING, which is what capping the backlog means. Below it is REPORTED with the number to lower it to: lowering is a one-word edit in the same commit as the ruling, and the report is what stops ground gained being quietly given back. ABSENT is a finding too — a cap you can delete is not a cap. It is a ratchet rather than a flat target because this check lists `unruled` at exit 0 on purpose: a check that fails from day one over a pre-existing backlog is a check that gets ignored, so a target of 10 against a live backlog of 32 would be permanently red and therefore disabled. Set to 32 = the measured count on 2026-08-23, before batch 1 is ratified. Precedent: 102_coverage_ratchet.txt.
_scan_baseline_doc: bugs_open/358. Codes that platform/orchestration/actions WRITES and this registry does not yet declare — the pre-existing backlog for findingcodes_scan_test.go's source-side early warning, which fails on anything NOT listed here. A RATCHET, for the same reason the unruled cap is one: a check that fails from day one over a pre-existing backlog is a check that gets ignored, and the crisp signal is 'someone just added a code nobody declared'. MEASURED 2026-08-24 when this was seeded: all 13 have fired ZERO times in the retained window, so the live-table check is blind to them BY CONSTRUCTION (its own stated blind spot: an unfired code produces no unread findings) — this list is precisely the population that blind spot leaves, which is why the scan is worth having at all. THE LIST MAY ONLY SHRINK: declare a code and delete its line in the same commit. An entry that is now declared is REPORTED as stale rather than failed, because a baseline that outlives its findings is how a check goes green by going blind.

CONTENT_LINK_REPAIR_DETAIL.why: Records what the link-repair pass DID on a build that SUCCEEDED, deliberately distinct from the blocker code because 'the two rows answer different questions' (validate_page_content.go). Its stated purpose is to name WHICH of three origins repaired, so a row that cannot say which path acted cannot spot the path that stopped acting. Comparing the three origins over time is a longitudinal question, and migration 567 gives it 365 days rather than the 30-day unresolved window this table's sweep otherwise applies — accepted knowingly. This records TODAY'S TRUTH, not the ambition: it is the code in this batch most worth a real reader (count by origin; an origin dropping to zero is the bugs_open/097 drift it exists to catch), and human-evidence is what 'nothing reads it yet' honestly says.

ACCEPTANCE_PREDICATE_NOT_EVALUABLE.why: Completion gate 1c could not evaluate an item's OWN stored acceptance predicate, so the item completed ungraded by it (bugs_open/395, CLM-024). Declared human-evidence for the same reason as its sibling NO_CHANGE_GATE_UNREADABLE_RESULT, which is the same shape one file along: no automated reader, and the rows are what a person reads when asking whether the gate is grading anything. ITS ONE INTERESTING PROPERTY, which is why it is worth writing at all: a stored predicate was evaluable AT EMISSION by construction (the emit gate refuses to store one that is not), so a row here means the page changed shape, the vocabulary moved, or THIS GATE HAS GONE BLIND — and if it fires on every item of an armed type it is the third, which otherwise wears the same face as the acceptable outcome 'no item carried a predicate'. Accepts the retention window it lives under (30 days unresolved, 14 resolved — migration 466; 365 days under 567): the blind-gate case is a standing property that re-fires on every completion, so a 30-day window cannot hide it.

LINK_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE.why: Caught undeclared by the daily check on its FIRST live run, 2026-08-24, ~2h after the code's first row. It records that a run could not establish what pages exist, deliberately distinct from 'this site has no pages' because the two have opposite remedies (bugs_closed/092). READER SHIPPED 2026-08-25 (bugs_open/392): discovery check `missing_prose_links` selects unresolved rows for the site it is running on, resolves each to its page, files an edit_live content_rewrite if the page still carries no writer-authored prose links, and resolves the row on a healed verdict only (resolved_by='missing_prose_links:<verdict>'). CORRECTION to this entry's previous text: it said these rows accept '30 days unresolved, 14 resolved — migration 466'. That is STALE. Migrations 567 and 580 removed the resolved-halves-life arm entirely; this code is not in 567's short-retention list, so its rows live 365 days whether resolved or not, and a consumer may resolve freely. The writer now also records page_name/page_id in context (2026-08-25) — the row's orchestration_id column does resolve the page, but orchestration rows are reaped while the row lives 365 days.
LINK_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE.note: Disposition flipped human-evidence -> consumed 2026-08-25 by the bugfix_392 lane, in the same commit as the reader (924079c94), council APPROVED corr 7d923ff6 round 2. The reader declares the code as a same-file const because the checker verifies the reader FILE contains the literal; the writer's const (prepare_link_context_action.go) is a deliberate duplicate across a package boundary. ⚠ THE READER IS COMMITTED BUT NOT YET RUNNING, and 'consumed' must not be read as 'draining' until it is. Raised by the council's editquality seat as an advisory objection and it is right: the Go is inert until the next fleet roll, and inert AGAIN after it until 'missing_prose_links' is named by hand in a live run_checks.config.checks array. Until BOTH have happened no code path reads these rows. Whoever completes those steps should replace this paragraph with the date they did. ⚠ CONSUMED IS NOT COVERAGE either: the reader only sees sites the discovery rotation visits, and the artefact half of that check is what actually finds link-less pages — 444 of 773 deployed pages under the check's own predicate as of 2026-08-25, against 2 rows this code has ever written.

CONTENT_LINK_SUPPRESSED_UNSHIPPED.why: Second code caught by the daily check on 2026-08-24, within an hour of its first row. Records that an href pointed at a page of this site that has never been served and is not arriving — deliberately distinct from the repair codes, which say 'this href pointed at nothing'. MEASURED 2026-08-24: no reader anywhere (Go, SQL, python, shell, live agent_definitions, scheduled_tasks). Accepts the retention window it lives under (30 days unresolved, 14 resolved — migration 466; 365 under 567). ⚠ ITS OWN DOC COMMENT IS 358 §3.1 HAPPENING LIVE: it introduces itself as 'a FOURTH code beside CONTENT_LINK_REPAIR_DETAIL, CONTENT_LINK_REPAIR_SKIPPED and CONTENT_DATA_LINK_AUDIT' and reasons from their record shape — which is exactly the propagation 358 measured, 'the record shape propagates; the missing reader propagates with it'. Three of those four are human-evidence today.
CONTENT_LINK_SUPPRESSED_UNSHIPPED.note: Declared by the bugs_open/358 lane, not by its author, for the same reason as LINK_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE: the check is red until a code is declared. The OWNER may overrule the disposition; the measurement behind it is not in doubt.

COMPONENT_FUNCTION_PIN_DIVERGENCE.note: bugs_open/388. The writer emitted a function name other than the one the pre-generation advisory pinned it to. HARMLESS BY CONSTRUCTION once the pin ships — the advised component_id already decided which row is written — and recorded precisely because it is harmless: it is the only durable meter of how often the model disagrees. Before the pin, obedience could only be sampled, and the sample was 11 observations with zero failures, which at n=11 bounds the disobedience rate no better than ~24% at 95% confidence. Compared against the ADVISED function, never against the final one, which may since have been site-suffixed by bugs_open/311's diversion. NOT deduped: the rate is the point. Review trigger: a sustained non-zero rate means the prompt pin has drifted from what the advisory emits and should be re-anchored.

COMPONENT_ADVISED_ROW_VANISHED.note: bugs_open/388. The advisory pinned a content_components row by id and, by store time, no non-forked row with that id existed — deleted, or turned into a fork, in the window between advice and store. The store falls back to the legacy by-function resolution, which is correct; doing so SILENTLY would not be, because this race is otherwise invisible and a silent fallback is indistinguishable from the pin never having been wired. Expected count is approximately zero. Review trigger: a sustained non-zero rate means the pin should carry a snapshot of the schema as well as an id, which is a follow-up round rather than a patch.

COMPONENT_PARALLEL_SECTION_BIRTH.note: bugs_open/388, and CLC-006's silent fork made loud. An UNPINNED creation on a section_type that already has an active non-forked section component. The field-contract guard cannot see this case at all — isRegeneration is false, so it is vacuous — which is why the duplicate is born with no error and no work item. Two such pairs exist in the live library from the generated route (tool-archetype-taster-quiz, tool-gripper-payload-calculator, both second rows born 2026-05-06 with function == section_type). Unrepresentable on the pinned path, so this fires only on the fail-open residual, which is what makes it worth counting. Diverted writes are excluded — a site-scoped twin is bugs_open/311 working as designed and already records COMPONENT_COLLISION_DIVERTED. The census is deliberately a DIFFERENT question (by section_type) from the one that resolved the identity (by id): bugs_open/324 shipped 32 dangling rows because its completeness check re-grepped the resolver's own patterns.

COMPONENT_UNPINNED_REGENERATION_AMBIGUOU.note: bugs_open/388, added in council round 2 on bug_historian's advisory objection that the un-pinned CREATE path was instrumented (COMPONENT_PARALLEL_SECTION_BIRTH) while the un-pinned REGENERATE path was not. This is the worse shape of the two: an existing row is OVERWRITTEN, and which one was decided by ORDER BY is_active DESC, updated_at DESC LIMIT 1 over a name that does not identify a row. [MEASURED 2026-08-25] 25 of 330 non-forked rows' function values carry more than one row (site-footer and site-header five each, spanning component_level 'section' AND 'site'), so the winner can change with no code change — anything touching a sibling's updated_at reorders the contest. Fires only when the count exceeds 1, so a row always means a real contest. Deliberately asks the question the resolver DISCARDS (how many were there) rather than the one it asked (which one wins): a LIMIT 1 structurally cannot report a contest, and bugs_open/324 shipped 32 dangling rows because its check re-ran the resolver's own query. Best-effort and never fatal — the row is written either way. Review trigger: a sustained non-zero rate means an un-pinned caller exists in practice and the pin should become required on that path.

WORK_ITEM_STATUS_OVERRIDE_REFUSED.note: bugs_open/396. FailWorkItemAction's `status_override` step-config key used to be honoured verbatim; it is now checked against workItemStatusOverrideAllowed and an unrecognised value is REFUSED, with the item falling through to the normal failure ladder. This row is what makes that refusal visible — it names the misconfigured STEP, not a failing item, which is why it is its own code rather than a generic one. OPERATIONAL rather than consumed: nothing selects by it, and its correct consumption is the generic newest-N diagnostic read of that agent's recent errors. It is expected to be RARE-to-never in practice — as of 2026-08-25 a recursive walk over every agent_definitions row (snapshots and soft-deleted included) found status_override on 4 steps in 3 agents and every value was 'needs_human_review', so nothing live can trigger it; a row appearing here means someone has configured a NEW value, which is exactly the event worth seeing.

SUBJECT_MISSING_ON_REPEATED_COMPONENT.why: Observe-only by design: the finding names a plan-shape defect a human reads, and no automated consumer exists yet (the entry's own note says 'Revisit disposition when an automated consumer exists'). Accepts the retention window it lives under (30 days unresolved, 14 resolved — migration 466; 365 days under 567) — acceptable here because the code is GATED on the plan carrying any subject at all, so it fires only on plans built after seed 640 and a lost row costs a re-observation on the next build rather than a lost fact. ADDED 2026-09-02 by the bugfix_394 lane, not by this entry's owner: the prose below was filed under `note`, which is the field the `consumed` shape reads, while the human-evidence arm reads `why` — so TestShippedRegistryIsSelfConsistent had been RED at HEAD for seven days, blocking a green run of the whole cmd/config-key-audit package. The original `note` is left exactly as written.
SUBJECT_MISSING_ON_REPEATED_COMPONENT.note: Structural half of planner rule 17 (seed 640, PBP-049): a repeated component with no subject on a subject-carrying plan gets identical briefs. Observe-only; GATED on the plan carrying any subject at all, so zero rows until seed 640 applies. Expected reader today: whoever drives 640 adoption and the apis.uk un-defer (council 4bd35ed8 r2 advisory, bug_historian). Revisit disposition when an automated consumer exists.

REPEATED_COMPONENT_BUILT_WITHOUT_SUBJECT.why: Observe-only by design: the build proceeded, and the row records that a page built N same-typed sections with no subject to tell the instances apart — identical briefs, near-duplicate output predicted (bugs_open/443: 11 of 11 such pages served real repetition, measured 2026-09-02). Expected reader today: whoever backfills subjects for the 443 cohort and the RFC_063 decision. Accepts the retention window it lives under (30 days unresolved, 14 resolved — migration 466; 365 days under 567): a lost row costs a re-observation on the next build of the same page, not a lost fact. Bounded: 25 repeat-layout pages fleet-wide as of 2026-09-02, one row per rebuild of one of them at worst. Revisit disposition when an automated consumer exists.
REPEATED_COMPONENT_BUILT_WITHOUT_SUBJECT.note: Build-side sibling of SUBJECT_MISSING_ON_REPEATED_COMPONENT (planner-side, write_site_plan, apis.uk lane): distinct code because the remedy differs — the planner one means the PLAN is malformed (replan / write subject rows, rule 17); this one means the page WAS BUILT with no subjects reachable at its serving tier (site_plan_sections.subject for planned sites; pages.section_subjects for plan-less pages, bugs_open/443). Deliberately NOT gated on the page carrying any subject: the pages this surfaces can never carry one.

LISTING_PAGE_HELD_NO_ITEM_SOURCE.why: The durable record that validate_site_plan's listing-source gate (opt-in, migration 720) HELD a listing page out of a plan because its item source resolved to zero — so 'the gate fired' and 'the planner proposed nothing unfillable' never produce identical evidence (bugs_open/444). The ACTIONABLE artefact is the paired capability_gap work item (item_key capability_gap:<page_type>:<page_name>, spec.gap_kind=producer_missing, spec.builder_needed names the enablement); this row is the gate's own audit trail. A lost row costs nothing operational — the work item is the receipt — so the retention window is accepted: 30 days unresolved, 14 resolved (migration 466; 365 days under 567).
LISTING_PAGE_HELD_NO_ITEM_SOURCE.note: One row per held page per plan run. Expected readers: the enablement operator answering a capability_gap (the row carries the same producer_needed slug), and anyone auditing why a planned page never appeared. Sibling of the gate's Warn logs, which do not survive pod restarts — the entire reason this durable row exists (the 444 diagnosis lost the build-time Warn lines to a restart).

TOOL_PAGE_HELD_NO_TOOL_SOURCE.why: The durable record that validate_site_plan's TOOL-source gate (opt-in key enforce_tool_sources, sibling of enforce_listing_sources) HELD a tool page out of a plan because no active component_level='tool' component exists on the site under any of the page's candidate function names. Without it, 'the gate held three tool pages' and 'the planner proposed no tool pages' are the same evidence. bugs_open/450: the planner names tool pages BEFORE their tools exist — tools arrive from the ~3h design rotation, later, under names the planner never saw (seotools.co.uk: 0 of 7 planned names matched what tool-deployer built) — so the planned page is one nothing will ever fill, and generic producers publish prose about the missing tool at a URL that serves 200. The ACTIONABLE artefact is the paired capability_gap work item (item_key capability_gap:tool:<page_name>, spec.builder_needed='tool-builder'), which deliberately co-dedups with builderForPageType's own unavailable-builder arm so one page yields one gap. This row is the gate's audit trail; losing one costs nothing operational.
TOOL_PAGE_HELD_NO_TOOL_SOURCE.note: One row per held page per plan run. ⚠ A hold is NOT a defect report about the tool pipeline: holding a planner tool stub starves nothing, because tool-deployer creates its own page rows under its own names and never reads planned tool pages (bugs_open/450 §7, measured at the rows 2026-09-03) — that measurement is the gate's licence to exist, and if it is ever falsified this gate is the thing to switch off. Sibling code LISTING_PAGE_HELD_NO_ITEM_SOURCE; sibling guard PBP-053, which stops such a page being FILLED where this stops it being PLANNED.
